script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Our heroine, JANE, a 30-something culinary mastermind, stands by a large prep table, chopping vegetables with practiced precision. She wears a crisp white apron, her hair is pulled back in a messy bun. The smell of fresh herbs and garlic wafts through the air.

Suddenly, JANE hears the sound of the door chime. She looks up and sees MARK, her new co-worker, enter. He's disheveled and carrying a takeout bag.

MARK
(cheerfully)
Hey, Jane! You're the legend around here, huh?

JANE
(smiling)
Hi, Mark. Welcome to the team. I'm just getting started on today's menu. Care for a bite to eat?

INT. KITCHEN - LATER

JANE and MARK sit at a small table, sharing a bowl of soup. They chat about their past experiences in the culinary world.

MARK
I've always loved cooking, but I never really had the opportunity to pursue it professionally. I've spent most of my career in sales.

JANE
(leaning in)
But you know what they say, it's never too late. I didn't start cooking until I was in my late twenties.

INT. RESTAURANT - NIGHT

The bustling restaurant is filled with the sounds of plates clattering and customers chatting. JANE and MARK work side by side, preparing for service. They bicker playfully about the proper way to chop an onion.

MARK
(laughing)
You really take this too seriously.

JANE
(grinning)
It's not a game, Mark. Precision is key in the kitchen.

INT. KITCHEN - LATE NIGHT

After hours of preparation and service, the kitchen is finally empty. JANE and MARK sit at the prep table, exhausted but satisfied.

MARK
You know, I really appreciate your mentorship, Jane. I don't think I would have made it through my first day without you.

JANE
(smiling)
It's the least I can do, Mark. We're all in this together.

INT. OFFICE - DAY

JANE sits at her desk, surrounded by recipe books and ingredient lists. She looks up as MARK enters, carrying a tray of fresh pastries.

MARK
I figured you could use a little pick-me-up.

JANE
(gratefully)
Mark, these look amazing. Thank you.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

The restaurant is bustling once again, and JANE and MARK work in perfect harmony. They laugh and joke as they cook, their friendship growing stronger with each passing day.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
